newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stock market halts decline, in poor volume.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stock market halts decline, in poor volume.

text.p: Jordanian shares held firm on Monday after a week of consecutive falls with minimal selling pressure in the absence of real investor demand, brokers said.
The official Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose 0.28 percent to 151.36 points, its first rise in a week of consecutive declines buttressed by weak selling pressure to drive prices lower.

"There was minimal supply of stock on offer with most of those in need of money already having sold..generally the selling pressure receded which helped stabilise prices," said broker Ibrahim Odeh, from Wataniyeh Financial Services.
Turnover was a low 289,358 dinars ($408,697) dominated by trade in a handful of stock with heavyweight Arab Bank alone accounting for nearly half of Monday's volume.
The bank rose 2.50 dinars to 253.50 dinars in trade worth 131,810 dinars.
Odeh said the market remains hampered by a liquidity crunch as a result of a tight monetary policy to bolster the dinar which is scaring away small investors.

Bearish sentiment continues to weigh down on the market which fell on Sunday to its four month levels in a recent pattern of poor across the board trade as outside buyers and institutional investors remain on the sidelines, brokers said.
Only a handful of stocks saw some trade, including Jordan Ceramic which was unchanged at 6.60 dinars and Jordan Wolsted Mill which rose 0.02 dinars to 6.82 dinars.

Among the busiest stock traded National Portfolio shed 0.05 dinars to 0.94 dinars in low trade worth 22,814 dinars and Jordan Electric Power fell 0.01 dinars to 1.65 dinars in minimal 11,871 dinars worth of trade.
Overall 19 shares fell while just seven rose. Another 10 were traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance rose 0.03 percent to 79.31 points, 4.90 percent down from the start of the year.
